subject: Re: MentorMix kickoff — status + preset trade-off
body:
Status:

- Reproduction done (a week late, 04-10 — my miss on the schedule, the mixup-weighting interaction took debugging). Quentin matched the published accuracy on the controlled web-noise benchmark within 0.5% at both the 20% and 40% noise levels, and confirmed the paper's headline: methods tuned on synthetic noise degrade much faster than MentorMix as real-world noise increases.
- Wanjiru's platform API is in review with the presets question open.

Trade-off needing a call: preset granularity. MentorMix's key hyperparameter tracks the (unknown) noise level; too few presets and users with 60%+ noise get bad defaults, too many and nobody knows what to pick. Proposal: three presets (low/med/high) plus an "estimate for me" mode that burns ~15% extra compute running a quick noise-estimation pass. Pilot team says they'd use the estimator.

Rec: ship all four. Cost is bounded and it kills the worst failure mode (confidently wrong preset).

Ondrej
